title: 2027-04-20-poc-scorecard-latency-throughput-debrief-with-orionx-analytics
summary: Weekly POC scorecard: Redwood presented 24h load window results vs customer's incumbent provider. Latency median improved ~18% on P50 for 512-token requests; tail (P95/P99) varied with burst profile. Throughput sustained at target w/ dynamic batching but cold-starts and KV cache misses created spikes. Action items: SE to run 10k request head-to-head, AE to send pricing for dedicated slots, customer to share exact traffic shape sample.
next_steps: Daniel to run 10k head-to-head run vs IncumbentAI and share CSV by 2027-04-23
Maya to share dedicated slot pricing + canary rollout plan by 2027-04-22
OrionX to upload representative traffic trace and sample payloads to the secure bucket by 2027-04-21
Schedule architecture deep-dive with SREs week of 2027-04-26
action_items: Daniel Ortiz: Run 10k sample head-to-head with IncumbentAI and produce latency distribution + raw logs (due 2027-04-23)
Maya Chen: Send dedicated slot pricing, SLA notes, and canary rollout checklist (due 2027-04-22)
Leila Hassan (OrionX): Share anonymized traffic trace and 1000 sample requests (due 2027-04-21)
Samir Patel (OrionX): Confirm compliance contacts for SOC2 questions and provide audit window (due 2027-04-25)
meeting_header:
Date: 2027-04-20
Time: 15:00 - 15:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: available
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Leila Hassan (OrionX Head of ML), Marco Reyes (Infra Lead), Priya Singh (Product), Samir Patel (SRE), Ava Kim (Data Eng)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. this is Maya at Redwood, i'm the AE, with Daniel our SE. quick check: can folks see my screen?
[00:10] Leila: Yep, we can. loud and clear.
[00:15] Daniel: cool. i'll kick off with the scorecard - we ran the 24 hour window as agreed, head-to-head against the incumbent stack you shared. quick note: some of the labels on our run show K-V cash misses — the auto transcribed it as "K-V cash" in the report, it's KV cache.
[00:32] Marco: bahaha, yeah thats what we saw in the csv too. we were mostly looking at P50 P95 and P99 across 128/512/1024 token profiles.
[00:42] Daniel: right. headline — for the 512-token profile the median latency improved about 18% vs incumbent, so P50 went from ~210ms to ~172ms on Redwood hosted profile. P95 improved ~12% but P99 is noisy during bursts, sometimes worse by 5-8% due to cold-start kernel picks.
[01:05] Priya: can you unpack the cold-start kernel thing? is that because you switch quant profiles?
[01:11] Daniel: partly. our runtime chooses kernels based on batch size and sequence length; when we see an unusual burst it can pick a fallback kernel until it compiles a faster path. that can cause a brief spike. we mitigated by warm-up and pre-compiled kernels in the dedicated flow.
[01:29] Leila: and what about throughput? we need sustained 250 rps at 512 tokens for peak periods. did you hit that?
[01:36] Daniel: sustained yes when batching is allowed - we saw sustained 260 rps with 4-8 request batching and prefix/KV cache hit rates above 70%. during the load test that replayed your burst pattern, the cache hit rate dropped to ~42% and throughput dipped to ~190 rps momentarily.
[01:58] Samir: that cache dip is concerning — that aligns with our production shape where 30% of requests are unique. can you tune cache TTLs?
[02:05] Daniel: yep. TTL and partial prefix caching are tunable. we also suggested a small LRU for the KV by request hash; we can push client-side sticky routing to increase local hit rate.
[02:19] Marco: sticky routing meaning what exactly? route by user shard?
[02:22] Daniel: route by user shard or request fingerprint so repeated sessions hit the same inference worker, increasing KV reuse. there's tradeoffs with load imbalance which we can mitigate with consistent hashing and background rebalancing.
[02:38] Priya: curious about quantization impact — in the notes you mentioned q4_0 vs q8_0? we haven't seen production regressions on quality but want to be cautious.
[02:47] Daniel: we used q4_0 on the dedicated candidate; it reduced mem and improved throughput about 15% with negligible quality delta on your eval set. q8_0 recovered some tail latencies for certain ops; there's a small hiccup for long-form generation but for your 512-token avg it's safe. we can A/B on a canary.
[03:05] Leila: ok. what about routing fallback? you had a playbook where when a model variant is overloaded you fall back to a cheaper variant instead of failing?
[03:12] Maya: yes — smart routing. policy can be latency-first or cost-first. we can set threshold-based fallback to a smaller quant model or a regional fallback to another pool. importantly we keep a pre-seeded KV snapshot for quick warmup to reduce miss spike time.
[03:30] Marco: we saw a couple P99 spikes in the evening window that matched your timestamp where fallback happened, but the fallbacks sometimes increased latency because they were cross-region.
[03:39] Daniel: thats a config issue; fallback should prefer same-region or reserved capacity slots. sounds like the rule used a global cheaper pool — we'll update the policy to prefer regional fallbacks, and add routing weight so it doesn't cross region unless necessary.
[03:55] Ava: was there any memory pressure or OOMs during the runs? we saw one worker that restarted in the SRE logs.
[04:01] Daniel: there was one OOM during the 03:00 UTC spike, tied to a background job the customer replay harness started. unrelated to inference but it impacted the node and caused a cold cache. we recommend isolating the test harness from inference workers or using cgroups.
[04:18] Leila: sounds reasonable. can you share the raw csv and the percentile plots? we have to sink them into our dashboard.
[04:24] Maya: yes — daniel will post the full CSV and a notebook with plots. we'll also include raw req/resp times and the run parameters (batch size distribution, cache hit rate series).
[04:36] Daniel: sending the head-to-head plot now. quick note on the head-to-head methodology: we replayed identical request order, same hardware class (A100-like), and matched model versions; the incumbent had a slightly different scheduling model which may explain some tail behavior. we logged kernel selection events for both.
[04:56] Leila: how confident are you the numbers are comparable? the incumbent claims their infra has a special network stack we can tune.
[05:03] Maya: fair question. we controlled for as much as possible but there are environmental delta's. that's why we propose you run the 10k direct hit from your environment hitting both endpoints — we'll run our endpoint and the incumbent's and compare with your auth tokens so net path is consistent.
[05:18] Priya: what's the lift for a dedicated slot? if we want reserved capacity to avoid kernel cold-starts and have predictable tail SLAs.
[05:25] Maya: dedicated slots are monthly commitments; i'll share a pricing sheet but rough numbers: a 4-slot reserved pool for your peak would be X$/month (Maya: note, will attach official pricing). slots give pre-warmed kernels, pinned models, and higher KV persistence.
[05:40] Marco: and can we burst beyond reserved if needed?
[05:43] Daniel: yes, we support burst capacity with autoscaling policies and short-lived spot slots. there's a configured burst budget to avoid noisy neighbors.
[05:52] Samir: security question — we need KMS/HSM integration for key wrapping and also audit logs retained 1 year. do you support that in private deploy?
[05:59] Maya: private deployments do. hosted can also integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping and we have an enterprise audit retention add-on. i'll attach SOC2 + audit docs.
[06:09] Leila: great. one more: can we get the per-token cost delta vs incumbent? we want to understand unit economics for scaling.
[06:17] Daniel: we computed per-token roughs — with batching and KV caching improvements Redwood unit cost was about 0.82x of incumbent on the 24h window. when cache hit falls below 50% the delta tightens to near-parity. we'll include a cost ladder in the CSV.
[06:33] Priya: in the plot I saw a weird mid-run step up in latency at ~14:23 UTC — any idea what triggered that?
[06:40] Daniel: that correlates with a scheduling window where our runtime GC kicked in on the node due to the background replay job. another reason to isolate harness.
[06:49] Marco: what's the recommended sticky strategy? user-shard, session-id, or ip-hash?
[06:54] Daniel: for your workload session-id works best since it groups conversational history; ip-hash can be noisy with large nat pools. we'll prototype session-id sticky routing in the next run.
[07:04] Leila: okay, let's talk about acceptance: our success criteria are P50 < 200ms and P95 < 350ms for 512 tokens sustained at 250rps. do you think Redwood can meet that with dedicated slots?
[07:17] Maya: yes — with a 4-slot reserved pool, tuned routing, and prefix caching we expect to meet that. Daniel: we'll validate in the head-to-head.
[07:27] Priya: timeline question: if we decide to go dedicated, how fast can you provision and do a canary?
[07:33] Maya: once contracts and payment done, provisioning is typically 3-5 business days for reserved slots; canary rollout can be executed in 24-48 hours after provisioning.
[07:43] Samir: are there logs we need to adjust on our side to make the CSV more useful? we want timestamps with microsec precision and request fingerprint.
[07:50] Daniel: microseconds for latencies yes, include request fingerprint and session id. if you can include a normalized timestamp and the request payload size that'll help correlate.
[08:02] Leila: can you run the 10k by Fri so we have something to show in our Monday exec sync?
[08:08] Daniel: yes we'll prioritize it and deliver the raw CSV + percentile plots by Fri 2027-04-23.
[08:14] Maya: i'll also follow up with pricing and the SLA note by 2027-04-22.
[08:18] Priya: perfect. any blockers?
[08:21] Marco: just the trace and auth to hit the incumbent + your endpoint. we'll get that to you by tomorrow.
[08:28] Leila: quick aside, we noticed a small generation quality mismatch on long completions in one sample — not a blocker but want to monitor.
[08:36] Daniel: we'll include the eval harness and diff outputs in the artifact share.
[08:40] Maya: ok let's recap next steps — daniel runs head-to-head 10k, maya sends pricing and SLA, orionx shares trace + creds, schedule SRE deep-dive week of 4/26. any edits?
[08:55] Leila: nope that covers it. thanks all.
[09:00] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll send the notes and artifacts after the call. bye.
